research.lane: Lane 1 — Is he doing "placement", and what does that trigger? (Code du travail, Livre III, Titre II & Titre III)
research.bottom_line: Yes, he is almost certainly inside the legal definition of activité de placement — but that is far less alarming than it sounds, because France deregulated private placement in 2010. There is no licence, no agrément, no déclaration préalable, no fee, no minimum capital and no qualification requirement. What the regime actually imposes on him is four things: (1) never take a centime from a candidate, directly or indirectly — 6 months' imprisonment and €3,750 under L5324-1; (2) never refuse service, to a candidate or an employer, on a discrimination ground, and never publish an offer that references one (L5321-2); (3) police the content of the offers he publishes — misleading offers carry 1 year and €37,500 under L5334-1, and that article puts the liability on the publisher whenever he acted without an express insertion request from the advertiser, which is the single most important design rule for his site; (4) send the préfet an annual statistical return before 31 March (R5323-7, R5323-8). His business model — free for candidates, employers pay for insertion and for visibility — is lawful: L5321-1 says placement "peut être exercée à titre lucratif", and L5331-1 expressly permits "l'insertion, à titre onéreux, d'offres ou de demandes d'emploi". His curation policy is also lawful: staff churn is not a discrimination ground. The three real traps are a candidate-side paywall of any kind, republishing offers he was not expressly asked to insert, and drifting into selecting candidates (RGPD + discrimination exposure) or into supplying staff (that is an entreprise de travail temporaire, which does need a declaration and a garantie financière).

findings.claim: The legal definition of activité de placement is broad enough to catch a site that merely publishes employers' offers
findings.detail: Article L5321-1 has three elements only: a service, supplied habitually, aimed at bringing offers and demands for employment closer together, by someone who does not become a party to the resulting employment relationship. The text names no requirement of selection, matching, shortlisting, or of a fee. 'Rapprocher' is the ordinary French verb for bringing two things together; a site whose entire purpose is that employers' offers reach candidates who then contact the employer is the paradigm case, not an edge case. The final clause — 'sans que la personne assurant cette activité ne devienne partie aux relations de travail' — is there to exclude the employer and the temp agency, not to exclude a passive publisher; it is a condition FOR being a placement operator, not against it. The second alinéa confirms the activity may be run for profit, which is why no licence attaches to it. Practical consequence: he should plan on the assumption that he is inside the regime, because the cost of that assumption is almost nil (see the declaration finding) while the cost of being wrong is criminal.
findings.source_quote: L'activité de placement consiste à fournir, à titre habituel, des services visant à rapprocher les offres et les demandes d'emploi, sans que la personne assurant cette activité ne devienne partie aux relations de travail susceptibles d'en découler. / La fourniture de services de placement peut être exercée à titre lucratif. Les entreprises de travail temporaire peuvent fournir des services de placement au sens du présent article.
findings.applies_to_him: Yes. Habitual, a service, aimed at rapprochement, and he never becomes the employer. All four elements met.
findings.penalty: None for being a placement operator as such — the regime is declaration-free since 2010.

findings.claim: The official statistical nomenclature explicitly classes online placement operators as placement agencies
findings.detail: INSEE's NAF rev.2 sub-class 78.10Z 'Activités des agences de placement de main-d'œuvre' lists, among what it comprises, online placement agencies. This is not law — an APE code has statistical value, not legal value — but it is the administration's own reading that doing this on a website does not take you out of the category. It is corroborating evidence for the broad reading of 'rapprocher' above.
findings.source_quote: les activités des agences de placement de main-d'œuvre en ligne
findings.applies_to_him: Corroborates that a pure online job board sits in the placement category. He may nonetheless register under 63.12Z (portails internet) like HelloWork — see the job-board finding.
findings.penalty: n/a

findings.claim: There is a contrary reading — a recent Versailles appeal decision is reported as requiring remuneration from the jobseeker before the placement qualification bites
findings.detail: A practitioner note on CA Versailles, 3 March 2026, RG 24/04425, reports the court as building the placement qualification out of habitual supply, intermediation between employers and jobseekers, AND compensation derived from the jobseekers. If that third element were truly part of the definition, a site that is free to candidates would fall outside L5321-1 entirely. I am reporting this with low confidence and flagging it as probably mis-stated: the 'paid by the jobseeker' element belongs to the OFFENCE in L5321-3 / L5324-1 (illicit paid placement), not to the definition in L5321-1, and the case concerned a training organisation, not a job board. I read the practitioner's summary, not the judgment. Do not rely on this to conclude he is outside the regime.
findings.source_quote: The court established that placement activity requires multiple conditions: habitual service provision, intermediation between employers and job seekers, and compensation deriving from job seekers. (CA Versailles 3 mars 2026 RG 24/04425)
findings.applies_to_him: If correct, he would be outside the regime. Treat as unreliable — build to the regime anyway.
findings.penalty: n/a

findings.claim: There is NO déclaration préalable. It was abolished in 2010. No form, no prefecture filing, no fee, no register
findings.detail: Until 2010, anyone whose main activity was placement had to send a prior declaration by registered letter to the préfet of the département of the registered office, at the latest the day before starting. Loi n° 2010-853 du 23 juillet 2010 (réseaux consulaires, commerce, artisanat et services) opened placement to any public or private body and removed that obligation, to comply with the EU Services Directive. The implementing regulatory articles (R5323-1 to R5323-6) were repealed by décret n° 2012-539 du 20 avril 2012. The Senate report on the bill records that article 14 deleted the whole Chapter III on private placement, moving up into Chapter I only the provisions compatible with EU law — which is exactly why the surviving obligations today are the gratuité rule and the non-discrimination rule, and nothing else. Concretely: he registers his micro-entreprise or company at the guichet unique like any other business, and that is the whole of his 'authorisation'. No professional qualification is required either.
findings.source_quote: Law n° 2010-853 of July 23, 2010 'ouvre l'exercice de l'activité de placement à tout organisme public ou privé' and suppressed the obligation of prior declaration to administrative authorities.
findings.applies_to_him: Directly. He has nothing to file before launching beyond his ordinary company/micro-entreprise registration.
findings.penalty: n/a — there is no longer an offence of undeclared placement.

findings.claim: The old rule that placement had to be your EXCLUSIVE lucrative activity was abolished by the same 2010 law
findings.detail: Before 2010 the supply of placement services was exclusive of any other for-profit activity, save recruitment advice and professional integration. Article 14 of the 2010 bill removed it, because the Services Directive very strictly limits any requirement to carry on an activity exclusively. Several third-party guides still repeat the old exclusivity rule — treat any source saying so as out of date. This matters to him: he can sell advertising, sponsorship, training content, a paid employer toolkit, or run an unrelated business alongside, without losing anything.
findings.source_quote: supprimer l'obligation d'exclusivité de l'activité de fourniture de services de placement lorsque cette activité est à but lucratif … contraires à la directive « services » … limite très strictement la possibilité d'exiger l'exercice exclusif d'une activité
findings.applies_to_him: Yes — his paid-visibility tiers and any side revenue are unaffected by placement law.
findings.penalty: n/a

findings.claim: The one recurring filing that survives: an annual statistical return to the préfet, due before 31 March
findings.detail: Two regulatory articles survived the 2010–2012 clear-out. R5323-7 states the general duty to send the préfet statistical information on the placement activity. R5323-8 sets the annual content and deadline: before 31 March of the following year, on a model fixed by ministerial arrêté — (1) placement turnover for the year past, expressed against total turnover where relevant; (2) the number of jobseekers, broken down by sex and age, received during the year, placed during the year, and on the organisation's files at 31 December. Note the oddity: since there is no declaration any more, no prefecture knows he exists, so nobody will chase him for it. The obligation is textually in force and is still listed as live by Bpifrance Création; enforcement in practice is effectively nil. His honest position is that he owes it, and that the cost of complying is one email a year.
findings.source_quote: L'organisme de droit privé exerçant une fonction de placement adresse au préfet chaque année, avant le 31 mars de l'année suivante, et selon un modèle fixé par arrêté du ministre chargé de l'emploi : 1° Le chiffre d'affaires relatif au placement, réalisé sur l'année écoulée, rapporté s'il y a lieu au chiffre d'affaire total ; 2° Le nombre des personnes à la recherche d'un emploi, réparties selon le sexe et l'âge : a) Reçues au cours de l'année ; b) Placées au cours de l'année ; c) Inscrites dans les fichiers de l'organisme au 31 décembre.
findings.applies_to_him: Yes if he accepts the placement qualification. Note he will struggle to report 'placées au cours de l'année' since he never sees the hire — report what he can and say so.
findings.penalty: No fine attaches to R5323-8 itself. Non-compliance feeds the L5323-1 / R5324-1 route: observations within 15 days, mise en demeure by registered letter, then closure of up to 3 months.

findings.claim: Gratuité: he may NEVER charge the worker, directly or indirectly. He MAY charge the employer
findings.detail: L5321-3 bans any direct or indirect retribution required from people looking for work in return for placement services. Only two exceptions exist in French law, neither of which is his: artistes du spectacle (L7121-9 code du travail) and agents sportifs (L222-6 code du sport). 'Indirecte' is the word to watch — it catches a premium candidate subscription, paid 'priority application', a paid CV review sold as improving his chances, a fee for early access to offers, a paid alert tier, an affiliate kickback taken out of the candidate's pocket, and a mandatory paid training bundled with access. The employer side is expressly open: L5321-1 says placement may be run for profit, and the Assemblée nationale's own impact study states that private agencies may charge employers while the public service remains free to them.
findings.source_quote: Aucune rétribution, directe ou indirecte, ne peut être exigée des personnes à la recherche d'un emploi en contrepartie de la fourniture de services de placement, sous réserve des dispositions : 1° De l'article L. 7121-9, relatives aux conditions de placement, à titre onéreux, des artistes du spectacle ; 2° De l'article L. 222-6 du code du sport, relatives aux conditions d'exercice de l'activité d'agent sportif.
findings.applies_to_him: Directly and permanently. His stated model (free for candidates, employers pay) complies. The rule constrains every future monetisation idea on the candidate side.
findings.penalty: L5324-1: six months' imprisonment and a €3,750 fine — 'Le fait d'exiger une rétribution, directe ou indirecte, des personnes à la recherche d'un emploi, en contrepartie de la fourniture de services de placement, en méconnaissance des dispositions de l'article L. 5321-3, est puni d'un emprisonnement de six mois et d'une amende de 3 750 euros.'

findings.claim: Selling job offers is forbidden whatever the medium — but charging an employer for the insertion is expressly permitted
findings.detail: L5331-1 is the article that makes his revenue model lawful and that would make a candidate paywall unlawful twice over. The prohibition bites on selling the offers themselves — which is what a paywalled listings site does to candidates. The second sentence carves out paid insertion: the employer buys the placement of its advertisement, which is precisely his product, including the higher-visibility tiers. The literal phrase 'dans une publication ou un autre moyen de communication payant' has been read as requiring a paid medium; the settled practice of every French job board, all free to candidates and paid by employers, is that the exception covers paid insertion in a free-to-read medium. I found no source, official or judicial, treating a free-to-candidate job board as breaching L5331-1.
findings.source_quote: Il est interdit de vendre des offres ou des demandes d'emploi, quel que soit le support utilisé. Toutefois, cette interdiction ne fait pas obstacle à l'insertion, à titre onéreux, d'offres ou de demandes d'emploi dans une publication ou un autre moyen de communication payant.
findings.applies_to_him: Yes. Employers paying for insertion and for visibility = the exception. Any candidate-facing paywall on the offers = the prohibition, plus the L5321-3 offence.
findings.penalty: L5331-1 carries no penalty of its own in L5334-1; the enforcement route for a candidate-side charge is L5324-1 (6 months + €3,750).

findings.claim: The heaviest penalty in this whole area is for publishing misleading offers — and it lands on the PUBLISHER when he acted without an express insertion request
findings.detail: L5331-3 forbids publishing, by any means of communication accessible to the public, a job offer containing false allegations or allegations likely to mislead, in particular as to (1) the existence, effective availability, origin, nature and description of the job offered, (2) the remuneration and ancillary benefits proposed, (3) the place of work. L5334-1 punishes that with one year's imprisonment and €37,500, and its third alinéa allocates liability: the advertiser who asked for the offer to be published answers for the offence; the director of publication or the service provider who communicated the offer to the public answers for it when he acted WITHOUT an express insertion request from the advertiser. This is the single most important architectural rule for his site. If every listing exists because a named restaurant or hotel expressly asked for it — signed CGV, an account, a submitted form, a paid order — the criminal risk on a misleading pay figure or a phantom vacancy sits with the establishment. If he scrapes, mirrors, or 'helpfully' re-posts offers he found elsewhere to fill the site at launch, the risk is his. In Megève, where seasonal offers routinely overstate pay, accommodation and hours, this is not a theoretical risk.
findings.source_quote: Le fait d'insérer une offre d'emploi ou une offre de travaux à domicile, en méconnaissance des dispositions de l'article L. 5331-3, est puni d'un emprisonnement d'un an et d'une amende de 37 500 euros. […] L'annonceur qui a demandé la diffusion de l'offre est responsable de l'infraction commise. Le directeur de la publication ou le fournisseur du service ayant communiqué l'offre au public est responsable lorsqu'il a agi sans demande expresse d'insertion de l'offre émanant de l'annonceur.
findings.applies_to_him: Directly and today, as a pure publisher. Never publish an offer without a traceable express request from the named establishment.
findings.penalty: One year's imprisonment and €37,500 (L5334-1, first alinéa).

findings.claim: Misleading claims about the free character of an employment-related service are the same offence — his 'free for candidates' promise must stay literally true
findings.detail: L5331-5 forbids publishing an insertion of service provision concerning job offers or careers containing false allegations or allegations likely to mislead, notably as to the free character of that service. L5334-1's second alinéa punishes it with the same one year and €37,500. Reading this together with the gratuité rule: advertising the site as free to candidates and then introducing any candidate-side charge is not merely the L5324-1 offence, it is also a €37,500 advertising offence. The 'free for candidates, forever' promise should therefore be written into his CGU as a commitment, not used as a marketing line he might later walk back.
findings.source_quote: Il est interdit de faire publier dans un journal, revue ou écrit périodique, ou de diffuser par tout autre moyen de communication accessible au public une insertion de prestation de services concernant les offres d'emploi ou les carrières et comportant des allégations fausses ou susceptibles d'induire en erreur, notamment sur le caractère gratuit de ce service.
findings.applies_to_him: Yes — his core marketing claim is exactly the claim this article polices.
findings.penalty: One year's imprisonment and €37,500 (L5334-1, second alinéa).

findings.claim: Non-discrimination binds him both as a gatekeeper and as a publisher — and his curation policy survives it
findings.detail: L5321-2 does two things. First, no placement service may be refused to a jobseeker OR to an employer on one of the discrimination grounds listed at L1132-1 (origin, sex, morals, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, family situation, pregnancy, genetic characteristics, real or supposed membership of an ethnic group, nation or alleged race, political opinions, union activity, religious convictions, physical appearance, family name, place of residence, bank domiciliation, state of health, loss of autonomy, disability, ability to express oneself in a language other than French). His door policy — admitting only houses he judges to offer decent conditions, quietly dropping those that churn staff — turns on none of those grounds, so it is lawful. Second, and this is the live duty: no offer he publishes may contain a reference to any of those characteristics. That means reviewing copy before it goes live. L5331-2 adds a specific prohibition on any upper age limit in an offer, except where fixed by law — a real risk in seasonal hospitality, where 'cherche jeune commis, 18-25 ans' is a common formulation.
findings.source_quote: Aucun service de placement ne peut être refusé à une personne à la recherche d'un emploi ou à un employeur fondé sur l'un des motifs de discrimination énumérés à l'article L. 1132-1. Aucune offre d'emploi ne peut comporter de référence à l'une des caractéristiques mentionnées à cet article.
findings.applies_to_him: Yes, today. His curation is safe; his offer-moderation process is the exposed part. Write the admission criteria down so a refusal can be shown to rest on staff-retention grounds.
findings.penalty: L5321-2 has no dedicated fine; enforcement runs through L5323-1 closure and through general discrimination law. L5331-2 (age limits) is not in L5334-1's list, but an age-referencing offer also breaches L5321-2.

findings.claim: Two small publication formalities: every offer must be dated, and anonymous offers require the employer's identity to be held
findings.detail: L5332-1: every published or distributed job offer is dated. Trivial to comply with and easy to forget — the date must be visible on the listing, not merely in his database. L5332-2: an employer who has an anonymous offer distributed by any means of communication accessible to the public must give his name or corporate name and his address to the director of the publication or the person responsible for the means of communication — that is him. And where the insertion is requested by an advertising agency, a selection body or any other intermediary, that intermediary must supply him the same details. So if he ever allows a hotel to post confidentially, he must still hold and be able to produce its identity. L5332-3 is not his, but is worth knowing: adverts for, and offers coming from, a temporary work agency must expressly state the agency's name and its character as an entreprise de travail temporaire — if he accepts listings from an interim agency serving the Megève season, that mention must appear.
findings.source_quote: Toute offre d'emploi publiée ou diffusée est datée. (L5332-1) — Tout employeur qui fait insérer […] une offre anonyme d'emploi fait connaître son nom ou sa raison sociale et son adresse au directeur de la publication ou au responsable du moyen de communication. (L5332-2)
findings.applies_to_him: Yes, today, as the person responsible for the means of communication.
findings.penalty: Not listed in L5334-1.

findings.claim: Offers must be written in French
findings.detail: L5331-4 forbids publishing, by any means of communication accessible to the public, a job offer whose text is written in a foreign language. The exceptions are narrow: where the job can only be designated by a foreign term with no French equivalent, the offer must carry a French description detailed enough to satisfy L5331-3; the rule applies to work performed in France whatever the nationality of the offer's author, and to work outside France where the author or the employer is French; and a publication written wholly or partly in a foreign language may receive offers in that language. In an alpine resort recruiting internationally, an English-only listing for a Megève season is not compliant.
findings.source_quote: Il est interdit de faire publier dans un journal, revue ou écrit périodique ou de diffuser par tout autre moyen de communication accessible au public une insertion d'offres d'emploi ou d'offres de travaux à domicile comportant un texte rédigé en langue étrangère.
findings.applies_to_him: Yes. If he wants to attract seasonal workers from abroad, the French text is the legal version and any English is a translation alongside it.
findings.penalty: Not listed among the offences in L5334-1.

findings.claim: Sanctions for operating outside the regime: administrative closure of up to three months, after a two-step mise en demeure; plus the L5324-1 criminal offence
findings.detail: L5323-1 gives labour inspection officers power to record breaches of Chapter I (that is, of L5321-1 to L5321-3 — the definition, non-discrimination and gratuité), and gives the administrative authority power, after a mise en demeure, to order the closure of the body concerned for a period not exceeding three months, where placement is carried on in breach of those provisions or where there is a breach of public order. R5324-1 sets out the procedure and is genuinely protective: the operator is invited to present observations within 15 days; beyond that, the préfet may issue a mise en demeure notified by registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt, setting out the breaches found; and only after a further period of not less than 15 days may the préfet order closure for up to three months. In other words, nobody shuts him down without first telling him in writing what is wrong and giving him at least a fortnight to fix it. The only criminal offence attached to the placement regime itself is L5324-1: charging the jobseeker — six months and €3,750. There is no offence of 'unlicensed placement' because there is no licence.
findings.source_quote: Lorsque l'activité de placement est exercée en méconnaissance de ces dispositions ou en cas d'atteinte à l'ordre public, l'autorité administrative peut, après mise en demeure, ordonner la fermeture de l'organisme en cause pour une durée n'excédant pas trois mois. (L5323-1) — l'organisme privé de placement est invité à présenter ses observations dans un délai de quinze jours […] Passé un délai qui ne peut être inférieur à quinze jours, le préfet peut ordonner la fermeture de l'organisme pour une durée n'excédant pas trois mois. (R5324-1)
findings.applies_to_him: Yes. Worst realistic administrative outcome is a warning letter and a fix window, not an ambush closure.
findings.penalty: Administrative: closure ≤ 3 months (L5323-1, R5324-1). Criminal: 6 months + €3,750 for charging jobseekers (L5324-1).

findings.claim: The line to an entreprise de travail temporaire is the only line with a real licensing gate behind it — and it is crossed by employing the worker
findings.detail: L1251-1 defines recourse to temporary work as the temporary making-available of an employee by a temporary work agency for the benefit of a user client, each mission producing two contracts: a contrat de mise à disposition between the agency and the user, and a contrat de mission, which is an employment contract, between the temporary worker and his employer, the agency. That is the trigger: the agency employs the worker. The moment he would hire a chef himself and place him in a hotel for a fortnight, or invoice a hotel per day worked for staff he pays, he becomes an ETT and everything changes. L1251-45: the activity of entrepreneur de travail temporaire may be carried on only after a declaration made to the administrative authority and the obtaining of a financial guarantee under L1251-49 — a further prior declaration is required if he moves his registered office or opens branches or agencies, and ceasing activity must also be declared. L1251-49 requires him to justify at all times a financial guarantee covering, in the event of his default, wages and accessories, statutory indemnities, mandatory social contributions and reimbursements due to social bodies. That is a capitalised, regulated business — genuinely out of reach for a 19-year-old micro-entrepreneur, and he should design deliberately to stay away from it.
findings.source_quote: L'activité d'entrepreneur de travail temporaire ne peut être exercée qu'après déclaration faite à l'autorité administrative et obtention d'une garantie financière conformément à l'article L. 1251-49.
findings.applies_to_him: Not today, and he must keep it that way. Never pay a worker. Never invoice per day worked. Never sign a contrat de mise à disposition.
findings.penalty: L1255-2: €3,750 fine for operating without the L1251-45 declaration or without the L1251-49 financial guarantee; récidive punished by six months' imprisonment and €7,500; the court may in addition ban him from temporary-work activity for two to ten years. L1255-1 punishes breach of the conditions of exercise of temporary work (L1251-2) with the same €3,750 / 6 months + €7,500 / 2-to-10-year ban.

findings.claim: The line between a job board and a cabinet de recrutement is NOT a licensing line — both are placement. What changes is data-protection and discrimination exposure
findings.detail: A recruitment firm that sources, screens and shortlists candidates for an employer, and invoices the employer a fee per hire, is doing exactly what L5321-1 defines and is subject to exactly the same regime as a job board: no licence, no declaration, no capital, fee from the employer lawful, fee from the candidate criminal. So the move from publishing offers to selecting candidates does not put him in a new legal category. What it does change is substantial nonetheless. (1) He becomes a data controller over a candidate file rather than a near-bystander: CNIL rules bite in full — only information allowing evaluation of the candidate's ability to do the job, a full information notice (controller identity, purposes, legal basis, which fields are mandatory, recipients, retention, rights), and retention capped at two years from last contact for candidates not taken on. (2) He personally becomes an actor in the hiring decision, so discrimination law attaches to his choices, not merely to the employers' wording — every rejection he makes becomes contestable. (3) A per-hire success fee requires him to know the hire happened, which means tracking outcomes, which means more data. The practical advice is that his 'we publish, the two sides talk' design is not just simpler to build, it is markedly lighter legally, and he should hold that line until he has reason not to.
findings.source_quote: Vous ne pouvez utiliser que des informations permettant d'apprécier la capacité des candidats à occuper l'emploi proposé ou de mesurer leurs aptitudes professionnelles. […] Conserver les CV et lettres de motivation pour constituer un vivier de candidats est possible à condition que la durée de conservation n'excède pas deux ans et que le candidat en ait été informé.
findings.applies_to_him: Today: light. He should keep applications off his servers — a mailto: or a link to the establishment's own form — so he never holds a CV. If he ever hosts applications, the CNIL regime applies in full.
findings.penalty: RGPD administrative fines (CNIL) — up to €20m or 4% of worldwide turnover under the general regime; in practice, for an operator this size, a mise en demeure first.

findings.claim: There is placement-specific data law too: no NIR, and a hard ceiling on how long jobseeker data may be kept
findings.detail: Alongside the general CNIL regime, articles R5323-9 to R5323-11 of the Code du travail apply specifically to private placement bodies: data concerning jobseekers may not be retained beyond six years after being recorded, and collection of the NIR (the social security number) is prohibited. Where the two regimes differ he should take the shorter and stricter: CNIL's two years from last contact for unsuccessful candidates, not the six-year outer limit. I read this on the Bpifrance Création page for regulated activities, which cites R5323-9 to R5323-11; I did not read the article texts themselves, so the precise wording is unverified.
findings.source_quote: Job seeker data cannot be retained beyond 6 years after recording. Collection of NIR (national identification numbers) is prohibited. References: Articles R5323-9 to R5323-11, Code du travail
findings.applies_to_him: Applies if he holds any jobseeker data. Never ask for a social security number — there is no reason a job board would.
findings.penalty: Enforcement via L5323-1 closure and via CNIL.

findings.claim: The big French job boards hold no placement declaration — because none exists to hold. Their company registrations show they class themselves as internet portals and software, not placement agencies
findings.detail: The question 'do Indeed France or HelloWork hold a placement declaration' has a clean answer: no operator in France holds one, because the declaration regime was abolished in 2010 and there is no register. The remaining signal is how they register their principal activity in the official company register, which I queried through the government's own API. HelloWork, SIREN 428843130, Rennes, carries APE 63.12Z — 'Portails Internet', whose INSEE definition covers operating websites with a portal function whose content is periodically updated. Indeed France SAS, SIREN 809675580, Paris, carries APE 62.01Z, computer programming. Neither carries 78.10Z, the placement-agency code that INSEE says expressly includes online placement agencies. Two caveats before he leans on this. First, the APE code is assigned by INSEE for statistical purposes and has no legal value — it does not determine whether an activity is placement. Second, choosing 63.12Z would not shield him if he were ever challenged; the qualification follows what he does. The useful conclusion is narrower and still worth having: the entire French job-board industry operates without any placement authorisation, nobody is checking, and registering as an internet portal is the market-standard choice.
findings.source_quote: HELLOWORK — SIREN: 428843130 — APE/NAF Code: 63.12Z — City: Rennes ; INDEED FRANCE SAS — SIREN: 809675580 — APE/NAF Code: 62.01Z — Paris
findings.applies_to_him: Strong practical signal. He can register under 63.12Z like HelloWork; the code does not change his obligations either way.
findings.penalty: n/a

findings.claim: Selling better visibility triggers a ranking-transparency duty under consumer law, with an administrative fine of up to €75,000 / €375,000
findings.detail: Article L111-7 of the code de la consommation defines an opérateur de plateforme en ligne as anyone offering professionally an online public communication service resting on either the ranking or referencing, by means of computer algorithms, of content, goods or services put online by third parties, or the bringing-together of several parties with a view to the sale of a good or the supply of a service. A site that ranks third-party job offers and sells higher placement in that ranking falls squarely inside the first branch. The duty is to give loyal, clear and transparent information on the general conditions of use, on the ranking methods, and on the existence of any contractual relationship, capital link or remuneration accruing to the operator where these influence the ranking. Article L131-4 sets the sanction: an administrative fine not exceeding €75,000 for a natural person and €375,000 for a legal person. Two limits on my confidence. I could not open an official page carrying the L111-7 text — economie.gouv.fr returned 403 and the INC page paraphrased rather than quoted — so the wording above comes from search summaries and secondary sources. And it is genuinely unsettled whether a jobseeker is a 'consommateur' such that the code de la consommation applies to this leg of his site. The mitigation is cheap enough that the uncertainty does not matter: a one-line, visible label on every boosted listing ('Offre sponsorisée') plus a short page explaining how listings are ordered and that paid visibility moves them up. Separately, the 'bonnes pratiques' duty of L111-7-1 applies only above five million unique monthly visitors and is self-regulatory — irrelevant to him.
findings.source_quote: Article L131-4 establishes that any violation of information obligations mentioned in articles L. 111-7, L. 111-7-2 and L. 111-7-3 of the Consumer Code is subject to an administrative fine that cannot exceed 75,000 euros for a natural person and 375,000 euros for a legal entity.
findings.applies_to_him: Probably yes, given he sells paid visibility. Label sponsored listings and publish the ranking rules — cheap, and it also builds the trust his whole positioning depends on.
findings.penalty: Administrative fine up to €75,000 (personne physique) / €375,000 (personne morale), article L131-4 code de la consommation. Unverified — I could not open an official source.

must_do: Assume he is a placement operator and build to the regime — the cost of that assumption is close to zero, since there is no licence, no declaration, no fee and no qualification requirement since the loi du 23 juillet 2010.

Never charge a candidate anything, directly or indirectly — no premium tier, no paid alerts, no paid CV review, no early access, no affiliate cut taken from the candidate. L5321-3, enforced by L5324-1 at six months' imprisonment and €3,750.

Publish no offer without a traceable, express insertion request from the named establishment — a signed CGV, an account, a submitted form, a paid order. This is what moves criminal liability for a misleading offer from him to the employer under the third alinéa of L5334-1 (1 year, €37,500). It also means: do not scrape or mirror offers from elsewhere to fill the site at launch.

Moderate the wording of every listing before it goes live: no reference to any L1132-1 discrimination ground (L5321-2), no upper age limit (L5331-2), French text (L5331-4), and a visible date on each offer (L5332-1). A short checklist in the employer submission form does most of this work.

Write his admission criteria down, in objective terms about working conditions and staff retention, and keep a note of why each refusal or delisting was made. His curation is lawful — staff churn is not a discrimination ground — but L5321-2 forbids refusing an employer on a discrimination ground, and a written standard is what proves he did not.

Keep the 'free for candidates' promise literally true and put it in the CGU as a binding commitment. Advertising it and later charging is not only the L5324-1 offence, it is a separate €37,500 advertising offence under L5331-5 / L5334-1.

Keep candidate applications off his servers at launch — send candidates to the establishment's own address or form so he never holds a CV. This keeps him out of the CNIL recruitment regime almost entirely. If he ever hosts applications: collect only what evaluates aptitude for the job, publish a full information notice, cap retention at two years from last contact, and never ask for a social security number.

Label every boosted listing visibly as sponsored, and publish a short page explaining how listings are ordered and that payment moves them up. Cheap insurance against article L111-7 of the code de la consommation (up to €75,000 / €375,000 under L131-4), and it is also the honest version of a site whose selling point is trustworthiness.

Calendar the annual statistical return to the préfet of Haute-Savoie, due before 31 March (R5323-7, R5323-8): placement turnover against total turnover, and the number of jobseekers by sex and age received, placed, and on file at 31 December. Report what he can actually measure and say plainly what he cannot.

Draw a bright line he will not cross: never employ or pay a worker, never invoice per day worked, never sign a contrat de mise à disposition. That is the entreprise de travail temporaire boundary (L1251-1), and it is the only boundary here with a real gate — declaration plus financial guarantee (L1251-45, L1251-49), enforced by L1255-2 at €3,750, €7,500 and six months on récidive, plus a two-to-ten-year ban.
unknowns: No court decision squarely on whether a pure job board — passive publication, free to candidates, paid by employers — is 'activité de placement' under L5321-1. I found none in either direction. The only decision that surfaced (CA Versailles, 3 March 2026, RG 24/04425) concerned a training organisation and is reported second-hand; I read a practitioner's summary, not the judgment.

Whether the R5323-7 / R5323-8 annual return to the préfet is in fact collected from anyone today. The declaration that would have told a prefecture the operator exists was abolished in 2010, leaving the reporting duty textually in force but with no intake channel. I found no arrêté fixing the current model form and no evidence of enforcement.
The exact current wording of R5323-9 to R5323-11 (six-year cap on jobseeker data, NIR prohibition). I have it only from the Bpifrance Création summary, not from the article texts.

Whether article L111-7 of the code de la consommation applies where the site's non-paying side is jobseekers rather than consumers buying something. economie.gouv.fr returned 403 and the INC page paraphrased; I could not open an official source carrying the L111-7 text or confirming the L131-4 amounts.

Legifrance refuses automated fetches, so I did not open it. Every Code du travail article quoted above was read on code.travail.gouv.fr (Code du travail numérique, Ministère du Travail), which does not always show a consolidation date — a lawyer should re-verify L5321-1 to L5321-3, L5323-1, L5324-1, L5331-1 to L5331-6, L5332-1 to L5332-3, L5334-1 and R5323-7 / R5323-8 / R5324-1 against Legifrance before he relies on them commercially.

Not covered in this lane and still open: his LCEN mentions légales obligations as a professional publisher — which, as with the Copius address problem, will force a contactable postal address into public view; his hébergeur-versus-éditeur status for the offers he hosts, which his curation arguably compromises; DSA obligations for an online platform hosting third-party content (most fall away below the small-enterprise threshold, but notice-and-action does not); and the CGV/contract terms governing his right to delist a paying establishment without publishing why.

research.lane: LANE 2 — Code du travail, Titre III "Diffusion et publicité des offres et demandes d'emploi" (L5331-1 à L5334-1), plus the adjacent Titre II "Placement" articles that decide whether Titre III's stricter regime bites. Researched 15 September 2026 against code.travail.gouv.fr (Code du travail numérique, official), entreprendre.service-public.gouv.fr, service-public.gouv.fr, DREETS Normandie, Conseil d'État, Sénat, CNIL, Arcom. Legifrance was not fetched (it refuses automated access); every codal text below was read on code.travail.gouv.fr, which reproduces it.

findings.claim: Selling job offers is banned; charging employers for the insertion is the express exception. His revenue model sits inside that exception, but the wording has a wrinkle.
findings.detail: L5331-1 is the first article of the Titre and it is about money. It bans selling offers or demands of employment on any medium, then carves out paid insertion. The ban is aimed at selling offers as a product (typically to jobseekers); selling advertising space to employers is the carve-out. The wrinkle: the carve-out literally reads 'dans une publication ou un autre moyen de communication payant' — a paid medium. A free-to-read website is not a 'moyen de communication payant' on a literal reading. Every French job board operates as he intends (free to read, employer pays), and the settled reading is that the ban targets trafficking in the offers themselves, not the sale of advertising space. Flagging it because it is the one article where his exact model meets the text head-on and a literal reader could quibble.
findings.source_quote: Il est interdit de vendre des offres ou des demandes d'emploi, quel que soit le support utilisé. Toutefois, cette interdiction ne fait pas obstacle à l'insertion, à titre onéreux, d'offres ou de demandes d'emploi dans une publication ou un autre moyen de communication payant.
findings.applies_to_him: Directly. Charging restaurants and hotels for listings, and more for visibility, is paid insertion and is the lawful side of this article. What he must never do is put any part of the offer content behind a paywall facing candidates — no paid tier that unlocks listings, no paid 'early access' to offers. That would be selling offers.
findings.penalty: Contravention de 3e classe (R5334-1). Article 131-13 3° du code pénal sets the 3rd-class maximum at 450 € — I did not open a page carrying that figure.

findings.claim: He can never charge candidates a centime, directly or indirectly. That is law, not a positioning choice.
findings.detail: L5321-3 forbids any direct or indirect remuneration being required from a person looking for work in return for placement services. The only exceptions are performing artists (L7121-9) and sports agents (article L222-6 du code du sport). Neither is him. Note 'indirecte' — a paid CV-writing add-on, a paid coaching upsell, or a paid 'boost my profile' tier sold to candidates all risk being indirect remuneration for the placement service.
findings.source_quote: No direct or indirect compensation may be required from job seekers in exchange for placement services (code.travail.gouv.fr rendering of L5321-3; the page returned the rule in translation, with the two exceptions L7121-9 and article L222-6 du code du sport).
findings.applies_to_him: His 'free for candidates, ever' is compliance, not generosity. It also closes off a whole monetisation lane permanently: 100% of revenue has to come from the employer side. Plan the business on that basis.
findings.penalty: Breaches of Chapitre Ier (placement) can be recorded by labour inspectors and, after mise en demeure, the administration can order the organisation closed for up to three months (L5323-1).

findings.claim: Every published offer must be dated. No exception.
findings.detail: L5332-1 is a single sentence and it is absolute. The service-public page for employers renders it as the offer having to show its 'date de publication ou de mise en ligne'.
findings.source_quote: Toute offre d'emploi publiée ou diffusée est datée.
findings.applies_to_him: A schema-level requirement on his listing model: a non-nullable published_at, rendered visibly on every listing card and detail page. This is one of the few Titre III duties that attaches to the act of diffusing, so it is his to enforce, not the employer's. Decide now what a 'bump for visibility' does to the date — re-dating a stale offer to buy it fresh placement is how a dating rule becomes a misleading-offer problem.
findings.penalty: Contravention de 3e classe (R5334-1), i.e. the 450 € maximum of article 131-13 3° du code pénal.

findings.claim: False or misleading offers are a délit carrying one year's imprisonment and a 37 500 € fine — and the code names exactly which three things it is watching.
findings.detail: L5331-3 bans publishing an offer containing 'allégations fausses ou susceptibles d'induire en erreur'. 'Susceptibles d'induire en erreur' is the operative half: no intent to deceive is needed, only a statement capable of misleading. The three enumerated heads are the ones that matter for hospitality: whether the job actually exists and is genuinely available; the pay and fringe benefits; and the place of work. 'Le caractère effectivement disponible' is pointed — a listing kept up after the post is filled, or a permanent 'always hiring' ad used as a CV funnel, is squarely in the text. Penalty from L5334-1.
findings.source_quote: Il est interdit de faire publier dans un journal, revue ou écrit périodique ou de diffuser par tout autre moyen de communication accessible au public une insertion d'offres d'emploi ou d'offres de travaux à domicile comportant des allégations fausses ou susceptibles d'induire en erreur et portant en particulier sur un ou plusieurs éléments suivants : 1° L'existence, le caractère effectivement disponible, l'origine, la nature et la description de l'emploi ou du travail à domicile offert ; 2° La rémunération et les avantages annexes proposés ; 3° Le lieu du travail.
findings.applies_to_him: Three concrete product consequences. (1) Seasonal hospitality churns — he needs an expiry and a 'poste pourvu' mechanism, because a stale listing attacks head 1°. (2) In Megève, logement and nourriture are the real currency; if a listing says 'logement fourni' it is an 'avantage annexe' under head 2° and must be true. (3) 'Lieu du travail' matters where a group runs several houses — the listing must say which one.
findings.penalty: Un an d'emprisonnement et 37 500 € d'amende (L5334-1).

findings.claim: THE ANSWER TO (c): liability is the employer's by default, and becomes HIS the moment he publishes without an express insertion request from that employer.
findings.detail: This is the load-bearing sentence of the whole Titre for him. L5334-1 closes with an explicit allocation rule. The advertiser who asked for the offer to be published carries the offence. The directeur de la publication or the service provider who communicated the offer to the public carries it instead when he acted without an express insertion request emanating from the advertiser. So it is not joint-and-several by default, and it is not a fault-based test about what he should have noticed — it turns on one binary fact: was there an express request to insert, from the advertiser, for this offer.
findings.source_quote: L'annonceur qui a demandé la diffusion de l'offre est responsable de l'infraction commise. Le directeur de la publication ou le fournisseur du service ayant communiqué l'offre au public est responsable lorsqu'il a agi sans demande expresse d'insertion de l'offre émanant de l'annonceur.
findings.applies_to_him: This makes or breaks the product. Safe: the employer fills the form, ticks a submit, and that submission is logged with a timestamp, an identified account and the exact text published. Dangerous, and it flips the criminal liability onto a 19-year-old: scraping or aggregating offers from other boards; importing a feed; a sales pitch where he writes the ad himself for a restaurant that only spoke to him on the phone; 'let me polish that for you' rewrites that change the job description, the pay or the location. Curating WHICH employers may list does not endanger him — that is a decision about the advertiser, not about publishing without a request. Writing or re-writing WHAT the listing says does endanger him.
findings.penalty: Whoever carries it: un an d'emprisonnement et 37 500 € d'amende for an L5331-3 breach; the same for an L5331-5 breach.

findings.claim: The enforcement body for misleading offers is the DGCCRF (répression des fraudes), not only the inspection du travail.
findings.detail: L5333-1 empowers agents de la concurrence, de la consommation et de la répression des fraudes to seek out and record breaches of L5331-3 (false or misleading offers) and L5331-5 (misleading service offers about jobs and careers), under the conditions of article L511-5 du code de la consommation.
findings.source_quote: Les agents de la concurrence, de la consommation et de la répression des fraudes sont habilités à rechercher et constater, dans les conditions prévues à l'article L. 511-5 du code de la consommation : 1° Les infractions aux dispositions de l'article L. 5331-3 ; 2° Les infractions aux dispositions de l'article L. 5331-5.
findings.applies_to_him: The realistic complaint path is a candidate who travelled to Megève for a job that did not exist, complaining to the DGCCRF. DGCCRF sweeps of online platforms are routine and public. His defence, when one lands, is the insertion-request log from the finding above — it is the single artefact that decides whether the file names him or the restaurant.
findings.penalty: Investigatory powers under article L511-5 du code de la consommation; the offence itself is the 1 an / 37 500 € of L5334-1.

findings.claim: Anonymous offers are allowed, but the employer must give HIM their name and address — and the administration and France Travail can demand it from him on simple request.
findings.detail: Two articles work together. L5332-2 obliges an employer publishing an anonymous offer to make their name or raison sociale and address known to the directeur de la publication or the responsable du moyen de communication — that is him. Where an advertising agency, a selection body or any other intermediary requests the insertion, the intermediary owes the same. L5332-4 then lets the administrative authority and France Travail (l'institution mentionnée à l'article L5312-1) obtain that name and address from him on simple demand, and use it to inform candidates. Note what is NOT required: nothing in Titre III obliges the employer's identity to appear in the advertisement itself. The disclosure runs to the publisher, not to the public.
findings.source_quote: Tout employeur qui fait insérer dans un journal, revue ou écrit périodique ou fait diffuser par tout autre moyen de communication accessible au public une offre anonyme d'emploi fait connaître son nom ou sa raison sociale et son adresse au directeur de la publication ou au responsable du moyen de communication. [...] Dans le cas d'offre anonyme, l'autorité administrative et les services de l'institution mentionnée à l'article L. 5312-1 peuvent, sur simple demande de leur part, obtenir du directeur de la publication ou du responsable du moyen de communication le nom ou la raison sociale et l'adresse de l'employeur.
findings.applies_to_him: He is the 'responsable du moyen de communication'. Two duties fall on him and neither is optional. (1) No anonymous listing goes live without verified legal name and address of the employer held on file — make it a required field in onboarding, not in the listing form. (2) He must be able to answer a DREETS or France Travail request quickly; build that as a lookup, not an archaeology dig. His curation model actually helps here: he already vets who may list. R5332-1 designates the administrative authority as the regional director (DREETS).
findings.penalty: L5332-2 is notably absent from R5334-1's list of articles carrying the 3rd-class fine — I found no specific penalty attached to it. Failure to answer an L5332-4 request would more likely be met with the closure power of L5323-1 or an obstruction charge.

findings.claim: (b) The French-language rule bites hard on a bilingual site: the ban is on diffusing an offer containing a text written in a foreign language, and it applies even when the job genuinely requires English.
findings.detail: L5331-4 prohibits publishing or diffusing an offer 'comportant un texte rédigé en langue étrangère'. Scope: services performed in France whatever the nationality of the author or employer, and services abroad where the author of the offer or the employer is French. The DREETS Normandie page is explicit that it applies 'peu importe que la parfaite connaissance d'une langue étrangère serait une des conditions requises pour tenir l'emploi proposé' — needing fluent English for the job is not a defence. Two carve-outs exist: where the job can only be designated by a foreign term with no French equivalent, the French text must carry a sufficiently detailed description so as not to mislead; and directors of publications and communication services that are themselves in a foreign language may receive offers in that language.
findings.source_quote: l'article L.5331-4 fait interdiction de faire publier dans un journal, revue ou écrit périodique ou de diffuser par tout autre moyen de communication accessible au public une insertion d'offres d'emploi [...] Lorsque l'emploi ou le travail offert ne peut être désigné que par un terme étranger sans correspondant en français, le texte français en comporte une description suffisamment détaillée
findings.applies_to_him: A bilingual FR/EN site is fine; an English-only listing is not. Architecture rule: French is the authoritative version of every single listing, always present and complete. An EN toggle is a translation sitting alongside it, never a substitute and never the only version an employer submits. This is a real product constraint in a resort where seasonal staff are often British or Eastern European and employers will want to post in English — the form must refuse an English-only submission. Anglicisms common in hospitality (runner, room service, night audit) need a French description beside them. The foreign-language-media carve-out is about publications edited in a foreign language and will not cover a French site with an EN mode.
findings.penalty: Contravention de 3e classe (R5334-1) — the 450 € maximum of article 131-13 3° du code pénal. As a breach of the act of diffusing, this one is realistically his exposure as much as the employer's.

findings.claim: No upper age limit may appear in an offer, and no offer may reference any of the 25-odd discrimination grounds of L1132-1.
findings.detail: Two prohibitions overlap. L5331-2 bans an offer stating 'une limite d'âge supérieure exigée du postulant', except where age conditions are imposed by legal provisions. L5321-2, in the placement chapter, adds a second sentence that is broader and blunter: 'Aucune offre d'emploi ne peut comporter de référence à l'une des caractéristiques mentionnées à cet article', the article being L1132-1 — origin, sex, mœurs, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, family situation or pregnancy, genetic characteristics, economic vulnerability, ethnicity/nation/race, political opinions, union activity, elected office, religious beliefs, physical appearance, family name, place of residence or bank domiciliation, health, loss of autonomy, disability, ability to speak a language other than French, whistleblower status. That last ground is worth a hospitality operator's attention: 'physical appearance' and 'place of residence' are live criteria in front-of-house recruitment.
findings.source_quote: Aucun service de placement ne peut être refusé à une personne à la recherche d'un emploi ou à un employeur fondé sur l'un des motifs de discrimination énumérés à l'article L. 1132-1. Aucune offre d'emploi ne peut comporter de référence à l'une des caractéristiques mentionnées à cet article.
findings.applies_to_him: Two things. (1) He needs a listing review step — automated keyword flags plus his own eye — because a Megève brasserie writing 'jeune fille souriante, bonne présentation, véhiculée, habitant la vallée' has put four prohibited references in one line and he is the one publishing it. (2) The first sentence of L5321-2 constrains his curation: he may not refuse service to an EMPLOYER on a discrimination ground. Refusing a house because it churns staff is not a listed ground and is lawful. Keep the refusal criteria written down and about working conditions, so the file shows what the decision was actually based on.
findings.penalty: L5331-2 breach: contravention de 3e classe (R5334-1). Discrimination proper: 3 ans d'emprisonnement et 45 000 € d'amende for an individual, 225 000 € for a legal person, plus publication of the decision — articles 225-1 à 225-4 du code pénal.

findings.claim: (d) There is no rule in Titre III about advertising jobs to minors. The real constraint is that ads for 16-18s in hospitality routinely describe work those minors cannot lawfully do — which converts into an L5331-3 misleading-offer problem.
findings.detail: I found no provision in L5331-1 to L5334-1, and none on the service-public employer page, creating a special regime for advertising to minors. What exists instead is a wall of substantive restrictions on employing them, and hospitality is the sector where they bite hardest. L4153-6: it is forbidden to employ or assign minors on a stage to bar service in débits de boissons à consommer sur place; the ban does not apply to the licensee's spouse and relatives to the fourth degree; and in débits de boissons AGRÉÉS it does not apply to minors over sixteen following a training programme with periods in the business leading to a qualification registered in the RNCP (L6113-5). L3163-2: night work is prohibited for young workers; a dérogation may be granted exceptionally by the inspecteur du travail for commercial establishments, but never between midnight and 4 a.m. L4153-1: no employment under sixteen, save apprenticeship, observation placements and end-of-compulsory-schooling training. L6222-1: apprenticeship runs from sixteen to twenty-nine révolus, or fifteen for those who have completed the first cycle of secondary education.
findings.source_quote: Il est interdit d'employer ou d'affecter des mineurs en stage au service du bar dans les débits de boissons à consommer sur place. [...] Dans les débits de boissons agréés, cette interdiction ne s'applique pas aux mineurs de plus de seize ans s'ils bénéficient d'une formation comportant une ou plusieurs périodes accomplies en entreprise leur permettant d'acquérir une qualification professionnelle sanctionnée par un diplôme ou un titre à finalité professionnelle enregistré dans le répertoire national des certifications professionnelles
findings.applies_to_him: This is the sharpest practical finding for his actual audience. A Megève bar listing 'apprenti barman, 17 ans accepté' is describing work that cannot lawfully be performed unless the establishment holds the agrément — which makes the offer's description of the job false under L5331-3 1°, and he is publishing it. Same for a listing promising a 17-year-old evening service that runs past midnight: no dérogation can reach past minuit. Build it into onboarding: for any listing open to under-18s in a débit de boissons, capture whether the house is agréé, and gate the shift-hours field so an under-18 listing cannot advertise work past midnight. His curation door is the right place for this — it is exactly the kind of thing 'houses I judge to offer decent conditions' should mean.
findings.penalty: No penalty attaches to him for the employment restrictions themselves — those are the employer's. His exposure is the derivative L5331-3 one: un an d'emprisonnement et 37 500 € d'amende, and only if he published without an express insertion request.

findings.claim: Positioning the whole site for young people is defensible; an individual ad with an age criterion generally is not.
findings.detail: L1133-2 says differences of treatment based on age are not discrimination when objectively and reasonably justified by a legitimate aim, 'notamment par le souci de préserver la santé ou la sécurité des travailleurs, de favoriser leur insertion professionnelle, d'assurer leur emploi, leur reclassement ou leur indemnisation', and where the means are necessary and appropriate. It expressly contemplates 'l'interdiction de l'accès à l'emploi ou la mise en place de conditions de travail spéciales en vue d'assurer la protection des jeunes'. 'Favoriser leur insertion professionnelle' is close to a description of his product. Confidence is medium because this is a justification standard applied case by case, not a safe harbour: no authority has blessed a job board aimed at young entrants, and the assessment would look at the site as a whole rather than at a slogan.
findings.source_quote: Les différences de traitement fondées sur l'âge ne constituent pas une discrimination lorsqu'elles sont objectivement et raisonnablement justifiées par un but légitime, notamment par le souci de préserver la santé ou la sécurité des travailleurs, de favoriser leur insertion professionnelle, d'assurer leur emploi, leur reclassement ou leur indemnisation en cas de perte d'emploi, et lorsque les moyens de réaliser ce but sont nécessaires et appropriés.
findings.applies_to_him: Draw the line between the site and the listings. The site may be aimed at young people entering the trade, may run apprenticeship-focused sections, may speak to 16-18s. The listings must not carry age criteria of their own, except where the age condition is imposed by law — an apprenticeship contract legitimately says 16 to 29 because L6222-1 says so, and L5331-2's own exception covers 'les offres qui fixent des conditions d'âge imposées par les dispositions légales'. A listing saying 'moins de 25 ans' for an ordinary CDI has no such backing.
findings.penalty: If a listing's age criterion is held discriminatory: 3 ans et 45 000 € (225-1 à 225-4 code pénal); an upper age limit specifically is also the 3rd-class contravention of R5334-1.

findings.claim: (e) TODAY: no obligation to state pay in a French job ad. But if a figure is stated it must be true — pay is one of the three enumerated heads of the misleading-offer offence.
findings.detail: I found no provision in Titre III, and none on the service-public employer page on preparing and diffusing an offer, requiring a salary or a range to be published. The employer page's own list of content requirements is: date, no false or misleading allegations, no discriminatory expressions, French. Pay disclosure is absent. What does exist is L5331-3 2°, 'La rémunération et les avantages annexes proposés' — one of the three items the code names as heads of the misleading-offer délit. So silence is lawful; an inaccurate or flattering figure is a délit.
findings.source_quote: 2° La rémunération et les avantages annexes proposés ;
findings.applies_to_him: For a hospitality board this matters more than the bare rule suggests, because the 'avantages annexes' are where seasonal offers are vaguest: logement, nourriture, indemnités de nourriture, pourboires, heures supplémentaires, prime de fin de saison. Anything he lets an employer put in a structured field becomes a published allegation about pay. Free text is safer for him than a tempting structured 'avantages' picker that invites optimistic ticking — or, better, keep the picker and make the employer confirm each item.

findings.claim: (e) COMING, and late: the EU pay-transparency directive's transposition deadline passed on 7 June 2026. France's bill reached the Conseil des ministres on 10 September 2026 — five days ago — and is not yet law.
findings.detail: Directive (UE) 2023/970 of 10 May 2023 on equal pay through pay transparency had a transposition deadline of 7 June 2026, per the Government's answer to a Senate question. France missed it. The Conseil d'État gave its avis on the transposing projet de loi on 23 July 2026; the bill was presented to the Conseil des ministres on 10 September 2026 and, per service-public, 'doit désormais être examiné par le Sénat et l'Assemblée nationale'. It was deposited at the Senate under procédure accélérée. So on 15 September 2026 there is no French pay-transparency obligation in force. Content of the bill, from the Conseil d'État avis: a new article L1221-9-1 du code du travail requiring the employer to give candidates 'une information sur une fourchette de rémunération initiale', and a prohibition, from article 5(2) of the directive, on asking a candidate for 'des informations sur des éléments relatifs à sa rémunération actuelle ou passée'. The Conseil d'État records that the recruitment-stage obligations apply to all employers, public and private; the size thresholds (50+, 100+ employees) govern the separate gap-reporting and joint pay assessment duties, not the candidate-information duty. A directive that is not transposed has no horizontal direct effect between private parties, so nothing binds a Megève restaurant today by force of the directive alone.
findings.source_quote: Dès la phase de recrutement, les employeurs devront informer les candidats à un emploi de la rémunération proposée ou d'une fourchette de rémunération. [...] ne pourront plus demander d'informations relatives à la rémunération actuelle ou passée des candidats.
findings.applies_to_him: The duty will land on the EMPLOYER, not on the job board. But the job board is the surface where a pay range physically has to appear, so it becomes his product problem regardless. Two build decisions to take now, while it costs nothing. (1) Add a pay-range field to the listing form — optional today, flipped to required the day the loi is promulgated. It also happens to be the single feature that most helps his stated purpose of steering young people to decent houses. (2) Never build a 'current salary' or 'salary expectations based on current pay' field into any candidate form — that question is on its way to being prohibited, and it has no upside for him. No size threshold will exempt his small clients from the candidate-information duty.
findings.penalty: Not yet determined — the penalty regime will be set by the loi de transposition, which has not been voted.

findings.claim: (f) There is NO obligation in Titre III to archive or keep published offers. The retention he actually needs is evidential, and it comes from the liability rule, not from an archiving duty.
findings.detail: I read the whole of Chapitre II, 'Conditions de publication et de diffusion des offres d'emploi', L5332-1 to L5332-5, plus R5332-1. None of them imposes a retention period or an archiving duty for offers. R5332-1 does nothing but designate the administrative authority of L5332-4 as the regional director (DREETS). The only retention hook in the chapter is L5332-5, which authorises décrets en Conseil d'État to set the conditions under which placement organisations may 'demander, détenir, conserver, diffuser et céder' nominative information — a power to regulate, not a duty to keep. What does create a de facto holding requirement is L5332-4: he must be able to produce an anonymous advertiser's name and address to the administration or France Travail on simple request, with no duration stated.
findings.source_quote: Des décrets en Conseil d'Etat déterminent les conditions d'application du présent chapitre, notamment, les conditions d'utilisation des informations nominatives que les organismes exerçant une activité de placement peuvent demander, détenir, conserver, diffuser et céder pour les besoins de cette activité.
findings.applies_to_him: The reason to archive is defensive, and it is the strongest operational recommendation in this brief. L5334-1 puts the offence on him unless he acted on an express insertion request from the advertiser. That means his archive of insertion requests IS his criminal defence, and its absence is the prosecution's case. Keep, per listing and immutably: the employer account identity, the exact text as submitted, the exact text as published, the timestamp of the express submission, every subsequent edit with its author, and the takedown. Retain at least through the prescription period for the délit. Separately, under CNIL guidance, a candidate's file may be kept two years after the last contact with the recruiter, subject to informing the person and obtaining their agreement — that governs candidate data if he ever stores applications, which on a pure publish-and-connect model he may be able to avoid entirely.
findings.penalty: No penalty for failing to archive — the risk is evidential, i.e. bearing the 1 an / 37 500 € of L5334-1 himself for want of proof.

findings.claim: CNIL: candidate data may be kept two years after the last contact, with information and agreement. His 16-18 audience is above the parental-consent threshold.
findings.detail: The CNIL's public answer on recruitment files gives two years after the last contact with the recruiter, longer with the person's formal agreement, and conditions retention on informing the person and obtaining their agreement. On minors, article 45 de la loi Informatique et Libertés requires, for online services processing based on non-contractual consent, that the holders of parental authority give their agreement jointly with the child's where the child is under fifteen.
findings.source_quote: Le dossier pourra être conservé 2 ans après votre dernier contact avec le recruteur, ou plus longtemps si vous avez donné votre accord formel.
findings.applies_to_him: His stated audience is 16-18, which sits above the fifteen-year threshold — those users can consent for themselves and he does not need parental consent machinery. The exposure is the edge: a 14-year-old signing up for a summer job. Either set a hard minimum age of fifteen on account creation, or build parental consent. Given L4153-1 forbids employing under-16s outside apprenticeship and observation placements anyway, a sixteen minimum on accounts is the cleaner design and removes the question.
findings.penalty: GDPR administrative fines; no criminal penalty from the code du travail.

findings.claim: As an online platform he owes DSA duties — but as a micro-enterprise he is exempt from the heavier tier.
findings.detail: Arcom, the French DSA regulator, lists the obligations for a small online platform: clear and intelligible terms of use, a contact point for authorities and for recipients of the service, notice-and-action mechanisms, and a statement of reasons for moderation decisions taken against users. It records that micro and small enterprises — fewer than 50 persons employed and under 10 million euros turnover — are exempt from obligations under articles 15(2), 19 and 29 of the DSA, which cover transparency reporting and the platform-specific operational requirements. Confidence is medium on the precise boundary of what survives the exemption; the Arcom page groups the obligations rather than mapping each to an article.
findings.source_quote: Micro and small enterprises ("moins de 50 personnes occupées et moins de 10 millions d'euros de chiffre d'affaires") are exempt from certain obligations under articles 15(2), 19, and 29 (Arcom page on DSA obligations and covered services).
findings.applies_to_him: A micro-entreprise is comfortably inside the exemption, so the heavy tier — transparency reports, internal complaint systems, trusted flaggers, the ban on profiling-based advertising to minors — does not apply to him yet. What does survive and what he should build anyway: published CGU, a named contact point, a way for anyone to report a listing, and a written reason given to an employer whose listing he pulls. That last one is worth noting against his 'silent standard' model: quietly ceasing to list a house is a moderation decision, and DSA article 17 logic points toward telling that user why. It does not require him to publish a rating or a public declaration — a private statement of reasons to the employer is the opposite of a public score.
findings.penalty: DSA enforcement sits with Arcom as Digital Services Coordinator; I did not open a page giving amounts for a platform this size.

findings.claim: He must carry mentions légales on the site, and the sanction is disproportionate to how easy it is to get right.
findings.detail: Under the loi n°2004-575 du 21 juin 2004 pour la confiance dans l'économie numérique, article 6, an entrepreneur individuel's site must show name, forename and address with the 'entrepreneur individuel' designation or the initials EI, registration number, email and telephone, VAT number where applicable, and the host's name or corporate name, address and telephone number. The service-public page gives the sanction as one year's imprisonment and a 75 000 € fine, referencing the LCEN article 6 and articles L131-1 à L131-6 du code de la consommation. Confidence is medium on the amount because the fetched page reported 75 000 € for an individual while the general search material also cited 375 000 € for companies, and I did not open a second page to reconcile the figures.
findings.source_quote: 1 an d'emprisonnement / 75 000 € d'amende (service-public page on mandatory mentions for an individual entrepreneur's website, citing Loi n°2004-575 du 21 juin 2004, article 6).
findings.applies_to_him: Trivial to comply with and easy to forget in a v1. Note it interacts with the Titre III duties: the mentions légales identify him as the responsable du moyen de communication, which is exactly the capacity in which L5332-2 and L5332-4 address him.

findings.claim: Selling a service to jobseekers while misdescribing it as free is its own délit, separate from the offers rules.
findings.detail: L5331-5 bans publishing or diffusing an insertion of a service provision concerning job offers or careers containing false or misleading allegations, 'notamment sur le caractère gratuit de ce service'. The code singles out gratuity claims by name. L5334-1 attaches the same one year and 37 500 € as for misleading offers, and L5333-1 gives the DGCCRF the same investigatory powers over it.
findings.source_quote: Il est interdit de faire publier dans un journal, revue ou écrit périodique, ou de diffuser par tout autre moyen de communication accessible au public une insertion de prestation de services concernant les offres d'emploi ou les carrières et comportant des allégations fausses ou susceptibles d'induire en erreur, notamment sur le caractère gratuit de ce service.
findings.applies_to_him: His 'FREE for candidates, no fee, ever' claim is a marketing promise that the code turns into a criminal representation. It is safe as long as it stays literally true — which, given L5321-3 forbids charging candidates at all, it must. The trap is a later pivot: if he ever adds a candidate-side paid feature while the homepage still says free, he has both breached L5321-3 and made a false gratuity allegation under L5331-5.
findings.penalty: Un an d'emprisonnement et 37 500 € d'amende (L5334-1).

findings.claim: IF THE PRODUCT DRIFTS into selecting or matching, the regime that changes is Titre II placement, not Titre III — and the exposure is closure, not just fines.
findings.detail: L5321-1 defines placement activity as providing, on a habitual basis, services aimed at bringing together job offers and job applications, without the provider becoming a party to the resulting employment relationship; it confirms placement may be carried on for profit. The definition is broad enough that a job board plausibly already falls inside it — 'rapprocher les offres et les demandes d'emploi' describes a listings site as readily as a recruiter. L5323-1 gives labour inspectors power to record breaches of Chapitre Ier and, where the placement activity is carried on in breach of those provisions or public order is harmed, lets the administration order the organisation closed for up to three months after a mise en demeure. Confidence is medium on whether he is inside the definition today; it is high that the answer stops mattering if he starts selecting, because the practices that trigger Chapitre Ier's prohibitions are the same either way.
findings.source_quote: L'activité de placement consiste à fournir, à titre habituel, des services visant à rapprocher les offres et les demandes d'emploi, sans que la personne assurant cette activité ne devienne partie aux relations de travail susceptibles d'en découler. La fourniture de services de placement peut être exercée à titre lucratif.
findings.applies_to_him: Reassuring news first: lucrative placement is lawful, so even if he is inside the definition he needs no special status, and per-hire fees charged to EMPLOYERS are not forbidden by anything I read. What changes if he drifts: (1) shortlisting or pre-screening candidates for a house makes L5321-2's non-discrimination duty operational rather than theoretical, because he is then making selection decisions about individuals on criteria he chose; (2) writing or editing the offers himself is what flips L5334-1's criminal liability onto him; (3) a per-hire fee charged to candidates is flatly unlawful under L5321-3. The bright line worth holding: decide about EMPLOYERS all he likes, never decide about CANDIDATES.
findings.penalty: Fermeture de l'organisme pour une durée n'excédant pas trois mois, after mise en demeure (L5323-1).

research.bottom_line:
Titre III is short, old and unusually kind to him — but only if one fact is always true.

The headline is L5334-1's last two sentences. Liability for a false or misleading offer falls on "l'annonceur qui a demandé la diffusion de l'offre" — the employer. It falls on the publisher instead when he "a agi sans demande expresse d'insertion de l'offre émanant de l'annonceur." That is not a negligence test and not joint liability. It turns on a single binary fact: did this specific listing come from an express request by this specific employer. So the answer to his question (c) is: the employer, by default, and him only if he publishes something nobody asked him to publish. Every design decision should protect that fact. An employer-fills-the-form product with a timestamped submission log is nearly untouchable. A product where he scrapes other boards, imports feeds, or helpfully writes the ad for a restaurant that phoned him is one where a 19-year-old carries a one-year prison exposure for a brasserie's lie. The log of insertion requests is not paperwork; it is his defence, and it is the real reason to archive, since nothing in Titre III requires archiving at all.
